requirement: Implement ParallelMetricsAggregator with multiprocessing Value and Array, process-safe atomic locking, category boundary validation, and clean worker joining.
skeleton: ParallelMetricsAggregator class using multiprocessing.Value and Array.
caption: A multiprocessing metrics aggregator built on shared memory primitives from the standard library. ParallelMetricsAggregator takes num_categories, defaulting to 10, and allocates a multiprocessing.Value of C int for the total and a multiprocessing.Array of C ints, one slot per category. record_batch validates the category index first, raising IndexError with a message naming the index and the valid range when it is negative or at or beyond num_categories, so an out-of-range write is refused with a clear error rather than failing inside the shared array. It then increments the total under total_count.get_lock() and the category slot under category_counts.get_lock(), each in its own with block, so concurrent workers in separate processes cannot lose an update. get_metrics reads the total and copies the array to a plain list, each under the matching lock, and returns a dict with total and categories. A module-level _simulation_worker function, importable by child processes, calls record_batch a fixed number of times for one category. run_parallel_simulation starts one multiprocessing.Process per worker, defaulting to 4, assigning category i modulo num_categories and passing the aggregator itself so the shared values are inherited, then joins each process with a two-second timeout, terminating and re-joining any straggler, and only after every join returns the metrics. Four workers at 2000 iterations each therefore report a total of exactly 8000, category sums that add to 8000, and 2000 in each touched category, a load heavy enough that an unlocked increment loses updates.

plan.intent: Aggregate counters from several processes without losing updates
constraints: Totals and per-category counts live in shared multiprocessing memory
An out-of-range category raises IndexError naming the valid range
Every increment and every read happens under the matching shared lock
Worker processes are joined with a timeout and a straggler is terminated
Four workers of 2000 iterations report exactly 8000 in total

rationale.teaches: Shared counters across processes with Value and Array updated under get_lock, bounds-checked category indexes, and worker joins before reading the totals.
rationale.why: A lost update under a race is probabilistic, so a fixture has to hammer the counter from several processes and check the exact total. Missing joins and missing bounds checks show up in the same run.

ops.docstring: Aggregate metrics from several processes through locked shared memory.

candidates.why_wrong: total_count is incremented without get_lock, so concurrent workers lose updates and the total comes up short.
category_counts is updated without its lock, so per-category totals are lost under contention.
Every non-zero category records a count of 0, so only category 0 ever accumulates.
Workers are never joined, so the metrics are read before the workers finish.
The category index is not bounds-checked, so an out-of-range index raises from inside the shared array instead of IndexError with a message.
